title: Abel summation of 1 − 2 + 3 − 4 + ⋯ = 1/4 (Geometric Series OQ-01/OQ-01/OQ-01)
problemStatement: Follow-up to the parent's Abel summation of Grandi's series (1−1+1−1+⋯ = 1/2): does the term-by-term derivative, Euler's series 1 − 2 + 3 − 4 + ⋯, have an Abel sum, and is it 1/4 = lim_{x→1⁻} ∑ (−1)ⁿ(n+1)xⁿ = lim_{x→1⁻} 1/(1+x)²? Resolved: yes.

insights: ∑ (−1)ⁿ(n+1)xⁿ = 1/(1+x)² for |x|<1 is the term-by-term derivative of Grandi's geometric series ∑ (−1)ⁿxⁿ = 1/(1+x).

The closed form can be derived WITHOUT differentiation, by adding Mathlib's ∑ n·yⁿ = y/(1−y)² (hasSum_coe_mul_geometric_of_norm_lt_one) and ∑ yⁿ = 1/(1−y) (hasSum_geometric_of_norm_lt_one) at y = −x, since n·yⁿ + yⁿ = (n+1)yⁿ and y/(1−y)² + 1/(1−y) = 1/(1−y)².
The Abel sum is the boundary value lim_{x→1⁻} 1/(1+x)² = 1/4, computed by Tendsto.inv₀ on x ↦ (1+x)² → 4 over the 𝓝[<]1 filter, mirroring the parent Grandi proof.
1/4 = η(−1) (Dirichlet eta), consistent via η(s) = (1 − 2¹⁻ˢ)ζ(s) with ζ(−1) = −1/12.
